cards.title: Refining antibiotic dosing regimens for the treatment of sepsis in critically ill patients in the intensive care unit.
cards.what: Critically ill patients experience significant and dynamic changes in physiology, risking suboptimal antibiotic exposure. Dose optimization strategies can help address this therapeutic gap.
cards.why: Dose optimization strategies can help address suboptimal antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients with sepsis.
cards.pkpd_hook: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic derangements affect antibiotic exposure in critically ill patients.
cards.source: PubMed, Expert review of clinical pharmacology
cards.original_title: Refining antibiotic dosing regimens for the treatment of sepsis in critically ill patients in the intensive care unit.
cards.headline: Optimizing antibiotic dosing for sepsis in critically ill patients

cards.title: Discovery of isoindolinone derivatives as potent, safe, and intravenously administrable NaV1.8 inhibitors for the treatment of pain.
cards.what: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.8 is primarily expressed in nociceptors in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and has emerged as a highly promising target for the development of non-addictive analgesics. Although the selective NaV1.8 inhibitor suzetrigine (VX-548) has demonstrated clinical efficacy, its poor physicochemical properties and significant CYP450 enzyme induction present challenges for intravenous administration and potential drug-drug interactions.
cards.why: Compound 3c exhibits potent inhibition of the NaV1.8 ion channel, improved solubility, favorable pharmacokinetic properties, and reduced CYP450 enzyme induction.
cards.pkpd_hook: Compound 3c has a half-life of 7.3 hours and clearance of 38.8 mL/min/kg.
cards.source: PubMed, European journal of medicinal chemistry
cards.original_title: Discovery of isoindolinone derivatives as potent, safe, and intravenously administrable NaV1.8 inhibitors for the treatment of pain.
cards.headline: New nav1.8 inhibitor compound 3c shows potent analgesia and improved safety

cards.title: Glepaglutide authorised in the EU for adults with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS)
cards.what: glepaglutide is indicated for the treatment of adults with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS). Patients should be stable following a period of intestinal adaptation after surgery.
cards.why: The European Medicines Agency authorizes glepaglutide for treating adults with Short Bowel Syndrome who are stable following intestinal adaptation after surgery.
cards.pkpd_hook: No pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic points mentioned in the abstract.

cards.headline: Glepaglutide approved in EU for adults with Short Bowel Syndrome
